title: Probe Prioritization Sprint Canvas for Prefetch Warmth
content:
Purpose:
This canvas captures a compact experiment plan to prioritize instrumentation and dashboard probes that improve visibility into prefetch / KV-cache warm paths. The goal for the sprint is to reduce investigation time for cold-cache latency spikes by 50% and provide a low-cost signal set suitable for multi-tenant rollouts.

Sprint goal (2 weeks):
- Ship 4 prioritized probes + 1 dashboard microkit.
- Validate probe fidelity on two canary tenants and measure query cost.
- Create a short runbook for cold-cache investigation.

Decision matrix (how we score probes):
- Criteria (weight):
  - Customer impact (weight 30) = reasoned by feature surface affected (latency-sensitive routes).
  - Signal fidelity (weight 25) = % of incidents where probe sheds light (historical / pilot).
  - Query cost (weight 15) = approximate monthly query expense at 10k qps normalized.
  - Implementation effort (weight 20) = engineer-days to instrument + deploy + test.
  - Investigation payoff (weight 10) = expected reduction in triage time (minutes).

Scoring example (0-5 per criterion, multiply by weight, sum -> priority score):
- Prefetch-hit-rate (lightweight event): 5*30 + 4*25 + 5*15 + 5*20 + 4*10 = 150 + 100 + 75 + 100 + 40 = 465
- Per-tenant-kv-eviction-rate (sampled): 4*30 + 3*25 + 2*15 + 3*20 + 3*10 = 120 + 75 + 30 + 60 + 30 = 315
- Cold-path-trace-anchor (trace spans): 5*30 + 5*25 + 1*15 + 2*20 + 5*10 = 150 + 125 + 15 + 40 + 50 = 380

Prioritized probes for the sprint (finalized):
1) Prefetch-hit-rate probe (global lightweight metric) — implement as counter & 1m rollup. Owner: Priya.
2) Cold-path-trace-anchor (request-scoped trace with prefetch span) — implement sampling policy for tail traces. Owner: Alex.
3) Per-route-first-token-time (quantile) — add 50/95/99 to dashboard. Owner: Liam.
4) Synthetic-prefetch-check (scheduled probe) — HTTP probe that simulates canonical prompt/payload to exercise cache. Owner: Maya.

Metric definitions (compact, copyable):
- metric: prefetch.hit.count
  - type: counter
  - description: increments when a request hits a prefetched KV entry (prefetch logic observed during routing).
  - calc: raw count aggregated per-minute, per-tenant, per-route
  - unit: requests
  - alert guide: sustained drop of >60% vs 7d baseline and p95 latency rising by >30% -> create P1 investigation.

- metric: prefetch.attempt.count
  - type: counter
  - description: attempts to prefetch (successful + queued).
  - calc: ratio prefetch.hit.count / prefetch.attempt.count = prefetch success rate
  - unit: ratio
  - owners: eng-serving-runtime, obs

- metric: route.first_token_ms
  - type: histogram (buckets + quantiles)
  - description: time from request arrival to first streaming token emitted by model runtime (includes routing + prefetch cost).
  - calc: 50/95/99 quantiles over 1m windows; label by route, tier, tenant
  - alert guide: p99 > 800ms for >5min on high-tier routes

- metric: kv.eviction.count
  - type: counter (sampled at 1/10 for low-cost tenants)
  - description: number of eviction events per-GPU-pool; used to infer cache churn
  - calc: normalized per-tenant per-hour
  - unit: evictions/hour

Tracing guidance (how we instrument spans and annotations):
- Important spans: inbound.http -> router.evaluate -> prefetch.enqueue -> prefetch.fetch -> runtime.kv.access -> runtime.generate
- Naming convention: service.operation[.sub] e.g., prefetch.fetch, runtime.kv.get, router.policy.eval
- Span tags to attach: tenant_id, route_id, request_id, prefetch_hint, kv_pool, node_id, sequence_len
- Trace sampling: tail-sampling at error/severity weight + probabilistic 0.2% for cold-cache route candidates. For prefetch probes prefer higher sampling (5%) during the experiment window.
- Trace anchor: mark the earliest runtime.kv.access for a request as "prefetch_anchor" tag so dashboards can link traces to probe metrics.

Dashboard microkit (layout and drill paths):
- Page: Prefetch Health (single page microdash)
  - Top row: 3 KPI cards: Prefetch success rate (1m), Route p95 first_token_ms, Synthetic probe success
  - Middle: Heatmap of prefetch.hit/count ratio by route vs hour of day (interactive time range)
  - Bottom left: Top-10 routes by delta p95 vs baseline (sparkline) with quick link to trace search for route_id
  - Bottom right: Eviction churn panel (per-pool stacked bars) + link to recent deployment tags
  - Drill links: Card -> trace explorer with filter "prefetch_anchor:true and route_id:<selected>"

Dashboard UX notes:
- Keep query windows small by default (1h) with quick presets (6h, 24h, 7d).
- Avoid high-cardinality grouping on default panels; surface per-tenant only behind a dropdown.
- Use derived metric panels (ratios computed server-side) to reduce live query cost.

Synthetic probe plan:
- Script: small canonical prompt that exercises a warm path and a forced cold path variant (unique prompt id forces miss).
- Frequency: 1 per 30s / region for canary tenants; 1 per 5m for global non-canary.
- Measurement: success boolean, first_token_ms, full-response-size, route chosen. Store as metric series and attach latest run ID to trace when present.

Investigation playbook (cold-cache latency spike):
1) Check Prefetch success rate KPI -> if dropping: go to heatmap by route/time.
2) Open top-affected route -> look at per-route first_token_ms p95 and synthetic probe results.
3) If synthetic indicates miss -> search traces filtered by prefetach_anchor:true and route_id.
4) From traces, check for long prefetch.fetch spans or high queue times (prefetch.enqueue).
5) If kv.eviction.count high -> inspect recent scaling or deployment activity; correlate with infra events (K8s node churn).
6) If no eviction evidence, sample full request payloads (obeying PI policy) and validate prefetch hint propagation.

Cost & query budget notes:
- Target probe rolling cost < $250/month for baseline rollout (across all tenants).
- Use aggregated 1m rollups and server-side derived ratios to keep Grafana/BI query volume low.
- Sample trace collection for detailed spans; prefer trace anchors with links rather than full-trace ingestion for every request.

Metrics rollout checklist (for each probe):
- [ ] Schema registered in metric catalog (name, owner, unit, retention)
- [ ] Instrumentation PR + integration tests
- [ ] Dashboard widgets implemented in microkit
- [ ] Canary validation on 2 tenants with pre/post comparison
- [ ] Runbook short doc + owner oncall handoff

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we add a lightweight per-tenant kv-warmth index without exploding cardinailty? (Priya to prototype sampled index)
- Determine whether synthetic probe should be able to toggle forced-miss at runtime for deeper experiments. (Maya)
- Agree on retention tiers for prefetch.* metrics (30d vs 90d) to balance trend detection vs cost.

Notes to implementers (quick tips):
- Add metric labels sparingly: route_id, tenant_tier, region are usually sufficient. Avoid tagging by model_version at high-cardinality.
- For trace spans, capture sequence_len only on samples to limit size.
- Write small unit tests that assert prefetch_hit increments when prefetch.fetch returns cached:true.

Links + references:
- Linked artifacts: CONFLUENCE-OBS-1245 (prefetch design notes), GH-PR-2043 (instrumentation helper), JIRA-OBS-582 (sprint epic)
